title: Threaded review map & pre-merge safety notes
content:
Purpose:
This is my personal scratchpad to map the important review threads for PR-4872 (redis patch + batching edge case). I want a low-friction mental model to hand off to reviewers and to keep a short rollback / mitigation plan in the PR description. Not polished — noisy, prioritized thoughts + quick checks.

High-level summary (one sentence):
- Changes routing in async batching path; introduces a small refactor that collapses two batchable states and relies on a new invariant 'kvReadyBeforeFlush'. Potentially fixes memory churn but risks a race when a streamed request cancels mid-batch.

Quick risk map (what could break in prod):
- Silent degrade: partial responses where streaming status header is missing (client-side show spinner forever).
- Latency regression under tail loads if the batching loop spins waiting on kvReadyBeforeFlush when GC/backpressure occurs.
- Rare crash: nil deref if ctx cancelled and cleanup callback runs concurrently with shared buffer free.

Top review threads to address (ordered by priority):
1) Cancellation / ctx handling
   - Look at batch_controller.go: handleCancelRace() new helper. Is it idempotent? Needs a unit test simulating ctx cancel + delayed flush.
   - Follow-up: add a debug metric for "cancel-before-flush" to surface count in staging.

2) Invariant correctness (kvReadyBeforeFlush)
   - Add short doc string in the code with expected lifecycle. Hard to infer from tests alone. Comment should say: when set, no writes to kv cache until flush completes.
   - Verify everywhere that toggles the flag uses defer to unset. Current code uses manual unsets in three places — fragile. Suggest centralize to a helper.

3) Observability gaps
   - No metric for "batch-wait-ms" in the new code path. Add a histogram and tag by request-type (chat/generation/embedding).
   - Log severity: debug vs warn. The line that emits "batch empty on flush" should be debug by default; promote to warn only if happened > 1% in 1m.

4) Tests / fuzzing
   - Unit: add deterministic test that simulates 50k micro-batches with random cancellations; assert no deadlocks and no leaked buffers (use testutils.CheckAllBuffersFreed()).
   - Integration: small load test on staging (10 workers) to measure tail latency before/after. Use the existing perf harness: scripts/load_test/async-batching.sh

5) Rollout plan notes (add to PR desc)
   - Canary: enable for 5% of traffic routed to hosting-eu region with routing policy tag "canary-async-v2".
   - Quick metrics to watch: 95/99/Max latency for generation, cancel-before-flush rate, "batch-wait-ms" p95.
   - Fallback: automatic traffic rebalancing to async-v1 if cancel-before-flush > 0.5% sustained for 3m.

Short revert / hotfix checklist (one-liners for oncall):
- Disable canary routing: update routing policy in console (route tag: canary-async-v2 -> remove).
- Patch: revert commit b3a7d1f (the refactor commit) and deploy hotfix-branch.
- Emergency guard: add per-worker flag ASYNC_BATCHING=false via env and restart workers in the pool.

Unresolved questions (to ping author):
- Why does flushPath choose to wait 30ms before drain? Is that experimental and tuned for GPU batching? (ping @Rina)
- Does the buffer allocator assume single-writer? There are spots guarded by atomic ops and others by mutex — mixed concurrency model needs explicit comment.

Micro-suggestions (small diffs):
- Replace manual flag toggles with: withKVReady(ctx, fn) helper that sets/unsets and returns fn's error.
- Replace three logs with structured fields: log.With("batch_id", id).Info("flush") to ease log correlation.
- Minor renaming: batchController -> batchCoordinator (namespace clash with controller package).

Work items I will do before sending for final review: (quick checklist)
- [ ] Add unit test simulating cancellation race (test_batch_cancel_race.go).
- [ ] Add a small histogram metric and increment call points.
- [ ] Add docstring + central helper for kv flag.
- [ ] Draft PR description section for canary + rollback steps.
- [ ] Add a comment linking to this scratchpad in the PR description.

Notes-to-self: style & tone to use in the PR description
- Be explicit about risk tradeoffs: memory reduction vs rare cancellation race.
- Call out that this is opt-in canary; not on by default.
- Attach guidance: how to run the local repro harness (scripts/repro/cancel-race.sh).

Example mini-repro steps (copied into PR):
1) run: GOFLAGS=-race go test ./batch -run TestCancelRace -count=1 -v \
   - this spins synthetic client/server in-proc and cancels mid-batch.
2) verify: no panics, no leaked buffers (use TEST_LEAKCHECK=1).
3) optional: run dockerized load: ./scripts/load_test/async-batching.sh --workers 4 --duration 60s

Loose timeline (for planning):
- today: finish unit test + central helper.
- +1 day: add metric + staging canary.
- +2 days: monitor metrics, iterate on failure guards.

Threaded TODO (quick links to line numbers to save reviewers time):
- batch_controller.go: lines ~172-214 (handleCancelRace)
- batch_loop.go: lines ~47-78 (flush timing)
- allocator.go: lines ~88-120 (buffer free path)

Random notes / heuristics I keep in mind for these PRs:
- Small helpers that reduce cognitive load are worth a few LOC if they remove ad-hoc cleanup.
- Observability is cheaper than perfect reasoning. If in doubt, add a metric at debug level.
- Tests that reproduce concurrency races are worth the extra 30-90 minutes; they catch 90% of these bugs early.

If you're reviewing this PR (quick checklist):
- Check the invariants: when kvReadyBeforeFlush is true, no write path touches cache.
- Run the TestCancelRace locally.
- Confirm metric names are consistent with naming guidelines (metrics.md).
- Suggest any immediate guardrails if you think this could affect production traffic quickly.

End — will paste a trimmed version of this into the PR description and link back to this scratchpad.

(Notes: messy and iterative — that's the point. I lean on reviewers for design nitpicks; explicitly calling out risks makes it easier for maintainers to vote for canary.)
